turns.prose: The canvas over the humming crate shivers in the dying light as Elder Maren braces the chest's corners, lifting it from under the stallkeeper's table; she nods to Ash and Vex to take the sides while Wren keeps watch. Ash steps close to Vex, keeping one hand on the chest's edge, and speaks low — dusk is here, the elder's set on the chest, and Ash stands by their word: settle the hum, then go together after the camp; don't strike out alone, the trail won't vanish in the time it takes to bell this thing. "Vex, the chest's hum is silenced and the elder's settled on belling it. You've been watching the square; tell me straight — did you see anyone else near the mechanism since I opened it? Before we chase a camp that may not be there, I want to know who's been fiddling with the works." "Wren, I see you scanning the square again — good habit, but the only new trouble here is that humming chest, and Elder Maren's about to carry it off. Leave the turnip crates alone; come help me keep an eye on her while she does." "Wren, don't go hunting trouble—we've got enough with that chest. Keep your eyes on the square; if anything moves, yell. I'll be the one checking the deer path after dusk." Vex scans the stalls once more — the fruit seller's shadow, the canvas ripples — then turns back to the chest, ready to take the side that Ash holds. Wren's gaze sweeps the far corners of the square for any new trouble, but the only movement is the stallkeeper's flap catching the wind.
